discovery.rule: Discovery prioritises companies, founders and buyers with a current request for help, consultancy, agency, contractor, freelancer or operational support. Networking/connection language alone is not a buying signal.
discovery.marketplace_rule: Treat marketplace names as discovery context, not proof of buying intent. A prospect still needs a current request/problem/trigger and must pass qualification.
discovery.surface_rule: Search surfaces are where people talk or expose a current requirement. Commerce platforms are context terms only. Do not treat a retailer or marketplace name as a search surface by itself.
signal_priority: explicitly asking for help / consultant / contractor / specialist
current operational problem with business impact
warehouse, 3PL, WMS, ERP or fulfilment change
hiring that exposes a current operational gap
funding, acquisition or rapid growth creating operational pressure
discovery.negative_signal_rule: Connection/networking posts without a current buyer-side need are not opportunities.

buyer_conversation_detector.purpose: Find recent first-person buyer-side conversations exposing a current ecommerce operational problem or an active request for help. Do not search primarily for service names or providers.
positive_requirements: speaker is experiencing the problem, represents the business, or is explicitly buying on its behalf
problem/request is current rather than hypothetical
ecommerce, marketplace, inventory, warehouse, 3PL, fulfilment or related operational context is present
ranking: explicit current request for a consultant/expert/help
current operational failure with measurable business impact
request for recommendation from an owner/operator
replacement/change of 3PL, warehouse, WMS, ERP or operational system
outgrown current process or excessive manual work
multichannel expansion causing a current operational gap
buyer_conversation_detector.freshness_rule: Live-opportunity search window is up to 30 days old. Reject results older than 30 days from the live lead feed. Prefer newer evidence when multiple results exist. Historical posts older than 30 days may only be used to improve search patterns and must never be presented as current opportunities.
buyer_conversation_detector.qualification_boundary: A matching conversation is DISCOVERED only. It cannot become CONTACT_READY until company identity, current need, ability to pay, decision-maker and usable contact route are independently verified.
rejection_rules: Reject new dropshipping store/build/setup/launch projects where the buyer primarily wants someone to build, finish, configure, populate or launch the store. Do not reject an established dropshipping business solely because it uses dropshipping; it may qualify when there is a current operational, inventory, supplier, order, marketplace, fulfilment or audit problem relevant to BT38.

discovery.search_method: Combine buyer-conversation patterns with commerce_context and search_surfaces. Prefer first-person posts/discussions from the buyer side. Suppress provider/service pages and generic job-board noise unless the listing exposes a credible consultancy/contract buying requirement. For the current commercial search, rank UK/Europe relevance above physical company/contact location: international companies and decision-makers are valid when the requirement includes UK/Europe operations, marketplaces or expansion.

direct_client.description: Ecommerce business with a current operational trigger or explicit request for help that could justify an independent audit or operational support.

live_paid_support.description: Company, founder or buyer currently seeking consultant, contractor, agency, freelancer or specialist help across ecommerce operations or marketplaces.
live_paid_support.qualification_rule: Must show a current requirement. Future/hypothetical networking or possible overflow is insufficient.

target_profile.geography: Primary commercial focus is UK/Europe relevance, not the physical location of the company or decision-maker. A company or contact may be based anywhere if the current requirement, marketplace scope, operational problem or expansion has a credible UK and/or European angle that Bhavin can support remotely. Do not reject a prospect solely because the decision-maker is outside the UK.
target_profile.business: ecommerce/DTC physical consumer products or businesses operating on relevant ecommerce marketplaces
geography_rules: Company headquarters or decision-maker location is context only, not a hard rejection gate.
Prioritise opportunities with a current UK or European ecommerce, marketplace, inventory, fulfilment, operations or expansion requirement.
A US, Canadian or other international company is valid when it is operating in, hiring for, launching into, or expanding across the UK/Europe.
A role covering multiple regions remains valid when UK/Europe is part of the scope.
Purely non-UK/non-European opportunities with no credible UK/Europe relevance should be lower priority or parked for later rather than presented as the strongest current lead.
The separate 3PL referral campaign remains UK-only until that campaign rule is deliberately changed.

reject_if: anonymous company with no resolvable buyer
generic networking with no current buying requirement
3PL placement only with no separate operational/audit need

search_signal_bias.purpose: Bias discovery toward buyer language that exposes an end-to-end ecommerce operational review requirement rather than generic ecommerce consultant keywords.
search_signal_bias.target_pattern: A real buyer describing current ecommerce systems, stock, fulfilment, reconciliation or workflow friction and seeking an external consultant/freelancer/project resource.
rules: Use these phrases as discovery signals, not proof of qualification.
Still require evidence dated within the 30-day freshness window.
Provider-side case studies and consultancy marketing are search-pattern evidence only, not buyer leads.
An old buyer post may teach the scanner useful wording but must not enter the live lead feed.
Commercial intent, capability, ability to pay and a usable decision-maker/contact route must still be investigated.

pattern_examples_only.example: Alex Shannon ecommerce systems/process consultant requirement
pattern_examples_only.reason: Strong buyer wording but outside the 30-day live-opportunity window.

linkedin_company_enrichment.purpose: When a LinkedIn buyer signal is found, enrich the prospect beyond LinkedIn so a free direct contact route can be used where available.
workflow: Identify the person and company from the LinkedIn post/profile.
Capture any company name, company page, website or other public company details available from LinkedIn.
Visit/research the company's official website and verify it is the same business.
Scan relevant public website pages such as Contact, About, Team, Footer and Terms for a legitimate business contact route.
Record a publicly listed business email when available; otherwise record the official contact form or other free business contact route.
Prefer a relevant named/company business email over generic contact forms when legitimately published.
Use the website to improve company-fit and commercial-scale research where supported by evidence.
Do not require paid LinkedIn messaging when a legitimate free direct route exists.
Do not automatically send outreach; prepare/record the route for user review.
contact_priority: paid InMail only if separately approved
linkedin_company_enrichment.budget_rule: Current outreach budget is £0. Prioritise legitimate free contact routes and conserve limited LinkedIn invitations.

recruiter_contact_lane.purpose: Treat recruiters and recruitment agencies as useful relationship/contact sources when they repeatedly see ecommerce, marketplace, Shopify, Amazon, operations, inventory, fulfilment or related client requirements.
workflow: When a recruiter posts a relevant role or contract, identify the recruitment agency and research what the agency does.
Where legitimately possible, investigate the underlying end-client as a separate potential buyer; do not assume or invent the client identity.
Keep the recruiter/agency as a contact source even when the advertised role itself is outside Bhavin's exact capability.
If a legitimate free contact route exists, a relationship message may be prepared explaining what Bhavin/BT38 does and the types of ecommerce operational requirements he can support.
The message does not need to apply for the advertised vacancy; it can introduce capability for present or future client requirements.
Do not automatically send any message. User reviews and sends outreach.
Record the source, agency, recruiter, relevant requirement, website and free contact route where available.
recruiter_contact_lane.positioning: Independent ecommerce operations and inventory auditing; marketplace operations; Amazon/eBay workflows; Shopify and connected ecommerce operations; warehouse/3PL, fulfilment, stock control, reconciliation, workflow/process review and practical implementation/support.
recruiter_contact_lane.outreach_budget: £0 - prioritise public business email, agency contact details and other legitimate free routes before paid LinkedIn messaging.

current_operating_note.strategy: Use text-first outreach when a recruiter publishes a legitimate direct mobile number. Target short-term, interim and project-based ecommerce operations work rather than permanent roles.
current_operating_note.handoff_goal: The recruiter opens and warms the opportunity; Bhavin takes over once there is a genuine operational requirement and an initial client conversation is appropriate.
current_operating_note.evidence_rule: A reply, CV request, portal registration or acknowledgement is useful engagement but is not proof of a live role. Treat a requirement as live only when the recruiter discusses an actual assignment, asks role-specific qualification questions, or offers a client conversation/introduction.
current_operating_note.cv_rule: Recruiter portals may require a CV. Use the recruiter-ready interim ecommerce operations profile; keep the consultancy-style profile for later explanation of approach.
current_operating_note.tracking_rule: Log every recruiter contacted, their response, CV/portal action, and next step in data/prospects.json. Do not duplicate records.

rules: Every completed outreach email must be presented as one complete copy/paste-ready block.
No manual assembly of recipient, subject, signature or body should be required.
Recipient email must be verified from a legitimate source and must never be guessed.
When Gmail sending is available and Bhavin explicitly asks to send an approved email, use bhavinrtailor@gmail.com.
Never auto-send outreach merely because a prospect was discovered or qualified.
For every strongest lead presented after research, prepare the finished send-ready outreach email in the same response without waiting for a separate draft request.

draft_email_format.trigger: When Bhavin asks for a draft email
draft_email_format.output: Show From, verified To, and Subject separately outside the copy block. Put ONLY the email body and signature inside the single copy/paste block.
draft_email_format.reason: Copying the body must not copy sender, recipient, or subject fields into the email message body.

generic_inbox_routing.rule: Generic inboxes are routed contacts, not direct contacts.
generic_inbox_routing.purpose: Make it obvious who the message is intended for so the recipient can forward it internally.
generic_inbox_routing.no_guessing: Do not invent a direct email when only a generic verified route exists.

unmonitored_inbox_rule.rule: If an automatic reply states that the recipient inbox is not actively monitored, may not be seen, or directs senders to other departments, do not treat the original route as a successful contact.
action: Record the original send and the automatic routing failure.
Use the organisation's explicitly provided monitored department address that best matches the enquiry.
Keep the intended decision-maker named in the subject when the replacement route is still a shared inbox.
Only mark the prospect as successfully CONTACTED after sending through a credible monitored route.
unmonitored_inbox_rule.no_spam_rule: Do not resend to every department. Choose the single department with the strongest relevance to the opportunity.

sender_display_rule.rule: Every prepared outreach draft must clearly show the sending account as 'Send from: bhavinrtailor@gmail.com' before the email draft so Bhavin does not need to switch between Gmail accounts to identify the correct sender.
sender_display_rule.note: This is separate from the email signature, which may also include the same contact email.

business_route_rule.rule: Do not use customer-service/support inboxes or helpdesk ticket forms for consultancy/business-development outreach unless the enquiry genuinely belongs there.
route_priority: free LinkedIn route to the decision-maker
reject_routes: customer help portal with no relevant business/commercial category
support ticket form intended for product/order/technical issues
business_route_rule.action: If the discovered route resolves to customer support or an inappropriate ticket form, mark it ROUTE_INVALID_FOR_OUTREACH and research a business-facing route before treating the lead as contacted.

sent_email_logging.rule: Any outreach email sent from this workflow/chat must immediately be recorded in the prospect/contact notes.
sent_email_logging.notes_requirement: Record that the email was sent, what it concerned, and the next follow-up action/date where appropriate.
sent_email_logging.no_duplicate_rule: Check existing notes before adding a sent-email event so the same send is not logged twice.

company_specific_email_design.rule: Every outreach email must be designed around how the recipient company actually operates, not generated as a generic template.
pre_draft_research: relevant sectors, markets, marketplaces or ecommerce disciplines
type of clients and projects handled
specific evidence creating the crossover with Bhavin's capability
company and role market scope, including any UK/Europe operation or expansion relevance; recipient physical location alone is not a rejection reason
drafting_rules: Use researched company-specific details in the opening and value proposition where relevant.
For recruiters, explicitly reference verified ecommerce/marketplace specialisms they recruit for rather than saying only 'ecommerce'.
For development/technology companies, explain how operational workflow design can sit alongside their technical delivery.
For direct buyers, focus on the buyer's stated pain point and current operation.
Never merely swap names into a generic template.
Keep the final email concise, one-click copy/paste ready and truthful.

3pl_referral_partner_lane.purpose: Treat suitable 3PL and fulfilment providers as referral partners who may already know which ecommerce brands have stock that has been sitting too long or is underperforming.
3pl_referral_partner_lane.commercial_angle: Do not lead by offering fulfilment or generic operational consulting that overlaps with the 3PL. Lead with slow/aged/underperforming stock: audit the existing listings and current sales channels first, then investigate additional marketplaces, sales channels, markets or commercial opportunities where appropriate.
3pl_referral_partner_lane.value_to_3pl: The 3PL keeps the fulfilment relationship. If more of the client's existing stock starts moving, the brand improves cash/stock movement and the 3PL can gain additional fulfilment activity.
capability: identify obvious listing or positioning weaknesses before recommending expansion
research additional marketplaces, sales channels and markets
support a referred brand directly once a genuine opportunity is identified
workflow: Research 3PLs that serve ecommerce/DTC brands and favour founder-led or relationship-led providers that already discuss growth, client strategy or partner referrals.

Find the strongest legitimate person to approach: founder, managing director, operations/client-services leader or partnerships/commercial lead. Do not default to a generic sales inbox when a direct person is available.
Use the opening problem: whether any brands have stock that has been sitting there for too long or is not moving as expected.
Explain that Bhavin can audit the existing listings and channels as well as explore new marketplaces, channels or markets; do not assume channel expansion is automatically the answer.
Make clear that the work is complementary to the 3PL relationship and is intended to help existing stock move.

If the 3PL identifies a brand that may benefit, qualify the actual problem before proposing work: stock age/quantity, current listings, current channels, product economics, restrictions and desired outcome.
Move a referred brand into its own prospect record when a real introduction or named opportunity exists.
Do not treat a positive acknowledgement from the 3PL as a live client opportunity unless a brand/problem is actually surfaced.
Log every sent email, response and next step in data/prospects.json and avoid duplicate records.
3pl_referral_partner_lane.outreach_positioning: Ask whether any brands they work with may benefit from help with stock that has been sitting too long or underperforming. Offer to audit how the products are currently listed and sold and to explore additional markets, sales channels or commercial opportunities if appropriate.

parked: Pulse Fulfilment - Sean Arslanian: no suitable direct route verified; LinkedIn message unavailable; do not force through generic sales inbox.
current_batch_note.rule: All contacted entries were confirmed sent by the user. Pulse remains parked until a legitimate direct decision-maker route is found.
researched_not_sent: Warehouse Republic - Mark Taylor (UK, active candidate)

message_design_rules: Lead with stock that has been sitting too long or is slow-moving.
Listing audits and current-channel audits are core. Do not mention international buying unless it is directly relevant.
State the mutual benefit truthfully: better sell-through for the brand and potentially more fulfilment activity for the 3PL.
Do not assume a warehouse wants stock removed to free space; tailor the benefit to the 3PL business model.
Position Bhavin as complementary to the existing fulfilment relationship, not a replacement.
Prefer a verified direct person or channel over a generic sales inbox.
For each researched lead, include verified contact details and one complete copy/paste-ready message.

current_campaign.rationale: The current test stays UK-focused because local founder-led 3PLs are an easier first route for trust, conversation, referrals and practical follow-up. Do not dilute the test with international outreach yet.
current_campaign.target: Founder/owner/MD-led UK 3PL and fulfilment businesses serving ecommerce/DTC brands.
current_campaign.batch_goal: Complete a controlled UK test batch before expanding internationally.
current_campaign.contact_rule: Only move UK prospects into active outreach during this campaign. Keep suitable non-UK prospects researched/parked for a later phase.
current_campaign.success_signal: A real brand/client problem, introduction, or conversation about slow-moving stock; acknowledgements alone do not prove the model.

pre_hire_operational_preparation_lane.purpose: Convert suitable live ecommerce/marketplace management vacancies into consultancy opportunities where the advertised role exposes a substantial operational handover, control, documentation or cross-functional coordination problem.
trigger_signals: new manager expected to diagnose or establish control
broad ownership across marketplaces, inventory, fulfilment, reporting, profitability or account health
multiple teams or external partners must be coordinated
incoming hire would otherwise need to untangle undocumented workflows or manual dependencies
30/60/90-day plan includes audit, diagnose, fix fundamentals, establish reporting, controls or roadmap
role combines operational clean-up with ongoing growth ownership
workflow: Confirm the role or requirement is currently live.
Research the company, scope, market coverage and person publicly connected to the requirement.

Complete the company profile briefing before presenting the opportunity: understand what the company does, ownership/parent structure, scale, channels, markets, and whether there is a realistic route into the business.
Assess whether the advertised responsibilities expose a pre-hire operational preparation problem rather than simply a normal vacancy.

Assess accessibility separately from commercial fit. Downgrade opportunities where the business is too corporate or there is no realistic decision-maker/contact route, even if the role itself is relevant.
Do not position Bhavin as applying for the role when the stronger fit is pre-hire preparation.
Offer to audit and structure the current operation before the incoming manager takes ownership.
Focus on documenting the current workflow, identifying gaps/risks/manual dependencies, establishing controls/reporting and setting priorities.
Explain the outcome as giving the incoming manager a clear controlled starting position so they can focus on growth/ownership rather than untangling the inherited operation.
Keep pricing, including the £999 audit, out of the first outreach unless the user explicitly chooses otherwise.
Use a verified free contact route and address the person connected to the role where appropriate.
After sending, immediately log the outreach in data/prospects.json and mark CONTACTED.

Work around the client's existing systems and tools first. Do not lead by adding or replacing software; the objective is to make the current operation clearer, more understandable and more controlled. Recommend new systems only when a genuine gap is established.
pre_hire_operational_preparation_lane.ranking_rule: Prioritise this lane when the role reveals an expensive or time-consuming operational handover problem and the company appears able to pay for a short defined audit/preparation project.
positioning_rules: Core positioning: audit and structure the operation around the systems already in place, reduce unnecessary manual/reactive work, and create a clearer understandable workflow before the incoming manager takes ownership.

company_profile_briefing.purpose: Prevent blind outreach. Before Bhavin is shown a prospect, provide enough commercial context to understand exactly who the company is, what it does, how it operates, and whether there is a realistic route into the business.
required_research: what the company sells or provides
main ecommerce channels and marketplaces where publicly verifiable
ownership or parent company where relevant
approximate business scale using public evidence such as employee range, revenue, funding, acquisition value or market presence when available
why the opportunity is relevant to Bhavin's audit/pre-hire workflow
who the likely decision-maker/problem owner is
whether that person appears realistically reachable through a legitimate free route
whether the organisation is too large, too corporate, too procurement-heavy or otherwise difficult to penetrate directly
whether a smaller subsidiary, brand, business unit or local operator offers a more realistic entry point
company_profile_briefing.presentation_rule: Do not present a lead as the strongest opportunity until the company profile briefing is complete enough for Bhavin to judge whether it is worth approaching. Once complete, immediately include the finished send-ready outreach email in the same result.
company_profile_briefing.accessibility_rule: A strong commercial fit is not automatically a strong lead. If the company is difficult to penetrate, heavily corporate, or the only route is generic recruitment/procurement with no credible decision-maker access, downgrade it even if the advertised problem is relevant.
company_profile_briefing.blind_application_rule: Do not encourage Bhavin to apply or outreach blindly based only on a vacancy. Research the company and route-in first.
company_profile_briefing.large_parent_rule: When a brand belongs to a large parent company, distinguish the brand-level opportunity from the parent-company structure. Prefer a reachable brand-level or regional operator where possible rather than treating the parent corporation as the target.

lead_presentation_workflow.rule: Every lead presented to Bhavin must include the completed company profile/research first and, immediately after it, a complete send-ready outreach email draft tailored to that exact company and opportunity.
sequence: Research and verify the live opportunity.
Complete the company profile briefing and accessibility assessment.
Identify and verify the strongest legitimate free contact route.
Draft the company-specific outreach email immediately after the research.
Present the research and the complete email draft together in the same result.
Do not require Bhavin to ask separately for a draft.
Do not auto-send; Bhavin decides whether to send.
email_requirements: Use the verified recipient email only; never guess an address.
Tailor the opening and value proposition to the company's actual operation and the current trigger.
Use the pre-hire operational preparation angle when that is the strongest fit.
Keep the first outreach concise and conversational.
Keep pricing out of the first email unless Bhavin explicitly asks to include it.
If no verified direct recipient email exists, use a verified official company email/contact route and address the relevant named decision-maker in the message where appropriate.
If there is no legitimate free contact route, do not fabricate one; downgrade the lead's accessibility and say so.
Phone formatting: for UK recipients use Mobile: 07774 257009. For international recipients use Mobile: 00 44 7774 257009.

For pre-hire operational preparation outreach, state where relevant that Bhavin works around the company's existing systems without introducing unnecessary new software, creating a clearer and more understandable workflow.

When the only verified contact route is a generic inbox such as sales@, hello@, info@ or contact@, the email subject must explicitly name the intended decision-maker so the message can be routed internally. Example: 'For Nathan Palmer — Before your Ecommerce Manager takes over'.
Clearly show 'Send from: bhavinrtailor@gmail.com' with every draft before the email block.
lead_presentation_workflow.presentation_rule: The single strongest result must be immediately actionable: company context, reason to pursue, contact route, and finished email draft should all be present before Bhavin decides whether to send.
